approach: Count Arithmetic Runs Ending at Each Index
explanation:
### How it works

An arithmetic slice ending at i extends an earlier slice when the last two differences match. In that case, the previous ending count gains one new length-three slice. Summing the ending counts counts every contiguous arithmetic slice once.

### Steps

1. Compare the two newest adjacent differences.
2. Set dp[i] = dp[i - 1] + 1 when they match, otherwise zero.
3. Sum all ending counts.

### Complexity

- Time: O(n).
- Space: O(n) for the shown DP arrays.

### Things to watch for

- Slices must be contiguous and contain at least three values.
- Equal values form arithmetic slices with difference zero.
- Reset the count when the difference changes.
